subject: Operational continuity: activation conditions, RTO/RPO, and data consistency
messages:
From: Sara Villanueva <sara@aureon-fin.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@aureon-fin.com, james.cole@aureon-fin.com
Date: 2026-05-28T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Aureon RFP - follow-up on continuity runbooks and data consistency requirements

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the initial packet. Procurement asked us to get a few clarifications before we mark Redwood as compliant on section 4.2 (continuity & failover). Two specific pieces they want documented for the RFP response:

1) Activation conditions and sequence: what exactly triggers a failover to EU-warm-standby versus rolling across zones? We need a short, ordered checklist we can include in our risk playbooks.

2) Data consistency guarantees at cutover: does Redwood provide any mechanism to ensure inference state (prefix/KV cache, session context) is preserved such that in-flight sessions don’t see token duplication or loss? If you have a short statement about eventual consistency vs streaming continuity that we can put in the RFP, that’d be ideal.

We have a deadline to include vendor clarifications by COB 2026-05-31. Can you confirm whether you can provide a runbook excerpt and an annotated RTO/RPO matrix?

Appreciate it — Sara

--
Sara Villanueva
Senior Sourcing Manager, Aureon Financial

To: sara@aureon-fin.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, procurement@aureon-fin.com

Hi Sara — looping in Evelyn and Markus for the detailed answers. High level: Redwood supports both automated region failover policies and manual activation. We can provide the ordered checklist you requested plus an RTO/RPO matrix.

Two quick clarifications from procurement: are you expecting stateful session handoff for long-running conversations, or is the ask limited to ensuring no data loss for persisted customer data (logs, audit trail, embeddings)?

We’ll draft the runbook excerpt and include an annotated diagram. Expect a follow-up today.

Best,
Ben

From: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
To: sara@aureon-fin.com
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, procurement@aureon-fin.com
Date: 2026-05-29T10:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aureon RFP - follow-up on continuity runbooks and data consistency requirements

Sara — thanks for the note and the deadline. Below is a concise, copy-ready response you can drop into the RFP (we’ll attach a slightly expanded runbook PDF and a swimlane diagram). I’ve put the short answers first and then a brief technical appendix for your engineering reviewers.

--- Copy-ready summary (short) ---
Redwood supports multi-tier failover with both automated and manual activation. Typical activation triggers include: sustained regional latency/availability degradation beyond configured SLOs, orchestration health checks failure, or explicit customer-initiated switchover for maintenance. In a warm-standby configuration:
- Recovery Time Objective (RTO) to regional availability: 5–15 minutes for stateless endpoints and 10–30 minutes for stateful inference sessions (dependent on session length and checkpoint cadence).
- Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for persisted customer data (logs, audit, embeddings): near-zero to 30 seconds with active cross-region replication enabled; default is 1–5 minutes for higher-throughput plans.
- For active session continuity: we offer optional session checkpointing that captures KV cache and conversation context at configurable intervals (default 15s). On switchover, the target region rehydrates the session from the most recent checkpoint; this minimizes token duplication/loss but may incur partial re-generation for tokens issued during the checkpoint window.

--- Technical appendix (short) ---
1) Activation sequence (ordered checklist)
   a) Detection: health probes and token-latency signals trigger alerting.
   b) Impact assessment: automated routing policy evaluates capacity and cost tiers across regions.
   c) Pre-failover snapshot: for stateful sessions, latest checkpoints (KV + session metadata) are marked for priority replication.
   d) Traffic steering: smart routing pushes new requests to standby region while existing in-flight requests are drained with connection-level grace periods.
   e) Rehydration & verification: target region pulls checkpoints, warms model caches (KV cache priming), and runs a short verification sweep using synthetic tokens.
   f) Final cutover: DNS and routing updates complete; monitoring entitlements verify latency/SLO compliance.

2) Data consistency and in-flight sessions
   - Checkpoint cadence: configurable; shorter cadence lowers RTO but increases replication cost.
   - KV cache durability: checkpoints persist both cache entries and inference metadata to the customer’s encryption-at-rest storage with cross-region replication.
   - Duplicate token mitigation: we mark checkpoint boundaries in session metadata so applications can detect and dedupe on client side; for most customers this prevents visible duplication.

3) Model variant fallbacks and compatibility
   - During failover we may route to a compatible model variant (same architecture, quantization profile). Responses include model-version headers for traceability.

Attachments included: runbook excerpt (PDF), swimlane diagram (Visio), annotated RTO/RPO CSV.

If you want, we can also provide a short statement for the audit appendix about retention of audit logs and access controls.

Would you prefer the copy-ready summary as a standalone one-paragraph statement for the RFP or the bulleted version above?

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Senior Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: James Cole <james.cole@aureon-fin.com>
To: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai
Cc: sara@aureon-fin.com, procurement@aureon-fin.com
Date: 2026-05-30T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Aureon RFP - follow-up on continuity runbooks and data consistency requirements

Evelyn / team — this is excellent and exactly what we need for the RFP. Two small asks before we close the section: one) can you provide a single-sentence audit-ready line we can include under "Operational Assurance" that spells out where audit logs are stored and for how long (we prefer a 12-month default for our templates); two) can you confirm the default checkpoint cadence and whether that requires a Dedicated plan (or available on Hosted API)?

On the latter: our security folks want to know if session checkpointing is a standard feature on the hosted plan or an enterprise add-on. If it’s an add-on, flag that in the line item and provide a short cost-exposure note.

If you can drop a one-paragraph insertion and attach the three files you mentioned, we’ll mark the RFP question closed.

Thanks — James
